jobs.title: Machine Learning Research Scientist and Engineer
jobs.description:
Company description

At Reward AI, we are building frontier intelligence for any robot. Our work brings together machine learning, robotics, and hardware to help robots learn from people and perform useful work across bodies, tasks, and environments. We welcome researchers, engineers, and people with experience in operations and product from a wide range of backgrounds.

Job description

Advance the models, data, and systems that help AI understand the world, reason, and act. This role spans foundational research and practical engineering, with opportunities across large language models (LLMs), vision-language models (VLMs), multimodal learning, foundation models, data engineering, and robot learning. Robotics-focused work includes imitation learning from human demonstrations, reinforcement learning, and policies that generalize across tasks and robot bodies. You could develop new modeling approaches, build data pipelines, scale training and inference, or create better ways to evaluate and improve models. Your work will contribute to Reward AI’s mission of building general robot intelligence, with a scope shaped around your strengths. Prior robotics experience is welcome but not required.

Responsibilities

Contribute across model research, data engineering, or ML systems, depending on your strengths and interests.
Develop and improve foundation models through pretraining, fine-tuning, post-training, or new approaches to learning and reasoning.
Explore robot learning methods such as imitation learning, behavior cloning, reinforcement learning, and learning from human video to develop generalizable manipulation and whole-body skills.
Build scalable pipelines for collecting, processing, curating, and serving diverse datasets, including text, images, video, and other modalities.
Design experiments and evaluations, analyze model behavior and data quality, and improve training or inference efficiency and reliability.
Collaborate with researchers and robotics engineers to evaluate models in simulation and on real robots, translate advances in general AI into useful capabilities, and shape technical priorities.

Preferred qualifications

A foundation in machine learning, computer science, data engineering, mathematics, or a related area, developed through study or practical work.
Experience in one or more of LLMs, VLMs, foundation models, multimodal learning, computer vision, imitation learning, reinforcement learning, robot learning, or data engineering. Depth in any one area is valuable; experience across all of them is not expected.
Strong programming skills and experience building models, data pipelines, or scalable software systems. Relevant tools may include Python, SQL, PyTorch, JAX, or distributed data processing frameworks.
Evidence of thoughtful research or strong engineering through projects, publications, open-source contributions, or deployed systems.
Curiosity, clear communication, and the ability to turn open-ended questions into concrete experiments.

jobs.title: Founding Engineer - Applied AI
jobs.description:
Help us keep water clean. Literally.

Nyad is on a mission to modernize how the world manages wastewater. Across thousands of factories and treatment plants, operators manually record data, collect samples, and conduct lab work. They make critical decisions that keep water clean, and when things go wrong, pollution spikes, and companies spend big on emergency measures.
With experienced operators retiring in the “silver tsunami”, a huge knowledge gap is opening. We’re building software tools for the operators that run the process. Biology meets machine learning and AI meets civil engineering, in one of the least digitized but most essential sectors on Earth.

Why this role matters

You’ll be part of Nyad’s founding team. As a founding engineer, you will help shape the product, the company, and the culture from the ground up. You’ll work directly with the founders to turn domain expertise into operator-ready tools.

What you’ll do

Collaborate closely with operators and engineers to understand real-world constraints.
Modeling & simulation:
Build and validate models that capture the operations or physical and biological wastewater processes.
Product development:
Translate engineering insight into intuitive software that operators actually use.
Deploy, test, and iterate in fast feedback loops with pilot customers.
Own the end-to-end lifecycle
from conception to production at scale.
Help define what Nyad builds next — roadmap, priorities, and product direction.

You might be a fit if you…

Have a background in mechanical, civil, or environmental engineering.
Have hands-on experience with modeling and simulation (process modeling, CFD, FEA, or similar).
Are comfortable working across the line between engineering analysis and software.
Thrive in ambiguity and can ship quickly without perfect specs.
Can communicate technical concepts clearly to non-engineers.
Are excited by mission-driven work and want your work to have a real-world impact.

Bonus points

Experience with wastewater treatment or industrial processes.
Familiarity with Python, simulation tools, or data analysis workflows.
Previous startup experience or a strong desire to thrive in one.
Comfortable talking to customers and gathering requirements in the field.

What we offer

True ownership; your decisions shape the product and company.
Equity that reflects your impact.
Direct exposure to cutting-edge environmental innovation and industrial customers.
The chance to build something that actually matters
.

jobs.title: Video/Image AI/ML Software Engineer - Graduate (Video and Edge, Multimedia Lab) - 2027 Start (PhD)
jobs.description:
Responsibilities

The Multimedia Lab builds highly efficient, scalable video codec hardware solutions (FPGA and ASIC) from the ground up, serving billions of users. We bring together algorithm, architecture, software, firmware, and hardware design and verification expertise, designing high-performance video silicon IP across ASIC and SoC digital design, verification, and next-generation video codec hardware. Alongside the silicon work, we advance research in video understanding, perceptual quality assessment, image and video enhancement, and intelligent coding, including using multimodal models to improve coding decisions.

Quality, efficiency, and speed rarely improve together. Sharper images and better perceived quality usually cost bitrate, compute, or latency, and a technique that works in research does not always survive production at global scale.

You will take ideas from research through to silicon and production systems, where research decisions show up in the cost and quality of video across ByteDance's products.

About The Team

Our team is building industry-leading, highly efficient and scalable video codec hardware solutions (FPGA and ASIC) from the ground up to better serve our billions of users. We are looking for strong software and firmware engineers to design algorithms, C-model, and firmware for advanced video encoding and processing implemented in dedicated hardware accelerators. The successful candidate will be part of a fast-growing team that includes algorithm, architecture, software, firmware, and hardware design and verification experts with a dedication to technical excellence and a passion to build large-scale and high-performing video platforms and services.

We are looking for talented individuals to join our team. As a graduate, you will get opportunities to pursue bold ideas, tackle complex challenges, and unlock limitless growth. Successful candidates must be able to commit to an onboarding date by the end of the year. Please state your availability and graduation date clearly in your resume.

Responsibilities:

Design video analysis (ROI, content understanding, feature extraction etc.) and quality assessment algorithms, and participate in database creation, algorithm design/development/optimization, etc.
Participate in designing strategy and solutions for E2E video quality optimization with a combination of video analysis, processing and encoding algorithms, such as frame-level rate control.
Apply designed algorithms for VOD / Live streaming monitoring, data analysis, objective evaluation for algorithms etc.
Collaborate with Infra and multi-media platform teams to integrate algorithms into production workflows and validate their impact through A/B testing.

Qualifications

Minimum Qualification(s)

Individuals who are completing or have recently completed a PhD degree in computer science, electrical engineering, mathematics, statistics or a related discipline.
Excellent programming, debugging, and optimization skills in one or more general-purpose programming languages, including but not limited to: C/C++, Python.
Knowledge of image/video analysis algorithms or subjective/objective image/video quality algorithms, and state-of-the-art technologies, such as VMAF, PSNR, SSIM etc.
Hands-on experience with machine learning or deep learning and familiarity with frameworks such as PyTorch or TensorFlow.

Preferred Qualification(s)

Research and hands-on experience in designing, training, or applying deep learning models, including CNNs, Transformer architectures, and multimodal large language models (MLLMs).
Knowledge of common video processing algorithms, such as super-resolution, diffusion model, etc.
Knowledge of video codecs (AVC, HEVC, AV1, VP9, etc.) and experience in video codec design.
Experience with embedded processors like ARM Cortex M0/M3/M4 or RISC-V architecture, and real-time development in an RTOS environment.
Great communication skills, eager to learn, and always passionate about turning cutting-edge technologies into real-life use cases.

jobs.title: Applied AI Engineer, People
jobs.description:
Atomic Machines is building the Matter Compiler™, the first in a new class of AI-native, all-digital manufacturing systems that build working machines directly from code. The Matter Compiler (MC) is aimed at micro-machines: motors and gears the size of a grain of sand, robots small enough to work inside the body, cooling built directly into the chips that run AI, and the many devices like them that have been waiting on a way to build them. Its first product is PrimeSwitch™, an electromechanical power relay the size of a button battery that carries 150 amps continuous current and opens in 50 microseconds, about a thousand times faster than a conventional contactor. Founded by Jeff Holden — serial entrepreneur, ex-Amazon SVP and Uber’s first Chief Product Officer — the company has raised $250 million to date.

Atomic Machines is based in the San Francisco Bay Area, with offices in Emeryville and Santa Clara.

About The Role:

This role reports to the Head of Strategic Growth and can be full-time or contract. You’ll be the first engineer embedded in our People team, working directly with leadership and building agents that reach every corner of the company. As we scale, there’s real opportunity to work across functions and embed with other teams.

Our goal is to build one of the first AI-native People Operations systems inside a scaling technology company. Instead of a large administrative HR organization, we’re building a small, high-leverage People team powered by smart systems, operational excellence, and AI-enabled processes we invent as we go.

Our People team knows our Atomizers (that’s what we call our people) but lacks the technical skills to build systems that scale our people practices. You’ll be the person who turns our ideas into working tools, uncovers redundancy, gets more out of the platforms we already use, and builds AI proficiency across the team. This role is about efficiency, clear metrics, and leaving the team more capable than you found it.

What You’ll Do:

Build agents and automations.
Ship agents and workflows across the employee lifecycle, from recruiting and onboarding to benefits and People Operations.
Shape our People tech stack.
Connect Greenhouse, Metaview, Justworks, Slack, and Google Workspace, define how People data flows between them, and get the most from what we already use.
Own People metrics and dashboards.
Build clear, trusted views of hiring pipeline, time to fill, recruiter capacity, headcount, and organizational health so leaders can make decisions quickly.
Find redundancy.
Map how our team actually works, spot repeated manual steps and tool overlap, and fix them.
Support a fast-scaling recruiting function.
Help us keep up with a high volume of open roles without losing quality or candidate experience.
Teach AI fluency.
Run hands-on sessions, write simple playbooks and build templates so non-technical teammates can use Claude, ChatGPT and agents confidently.
Keep exploring.
Stay on top of new AI tools and practices, test them, and bring forward what's actually useful.
Handle data responsibly.
Treat employee and candidate data with the care and confidentiality it needs.

What You Bring:

A bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Data Science, Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent hands-on experience.
1–2 years of experience, including internships or substantial projects, building AI agents or LLM-powered workflows that can scale across an organization.
Strong proficiency with Claude Code, plus comfort with Python, SQL and APIs.
Experience building dashboards or reporting from messy data.
A track record of building efficient, repeatable practices that scale, not one-off scripts.
The ability to explain technical ideas in plain language to non-engineers, and patience teaching them.
Curiosity about how teams work, and a habit of asking "why do we do it this way?"
Good judgment about privacy and handling sensitive information.

Nice to Have:

Familiarity with both Claude and ChatGPT ecosystems, including MCP connectors, custom GPTs or Projects.
Experience with workflow tools or BI platforms.
Interest in people operations, talent, or organizational design.

Why Join:

You'll build agents that reach every team in the company, with real ownership from day one.
Your work will shape how a fast-growing deep-tech company hires and supports its people.
You'll have the space to experiment with the newest AI tools and see your impact right away.

The compensation for this position also includes equity and benefits.

Salary Range: $110,000 USD - $150,000 USD

jobs.title: Field Application Engineer, AI Cloud
jobs.description:
About Bitdeer

Bitdeer is a world-leading technology company for AI and Bitcoin mining infrastructure.

Bitdeer is committed to providing comprehensive Bitcoin mining solutions for its customers and building AI computational infrastructure to support the AI revolution. Bitdeer handles complex processes involved in computing such as equipment procurement, transport logistics, data center design and construction, equipment management, and daily operations. Bitdeer also offers advanced cloud capabilities to customers with high demand for artificial intelligence.

Headquartered in Singapore, Bitdeer has deployed data centers across multiple countries, including the United States, Norway, Bhutan, and Ethiopia.

To learn more, visit https://ir.bitdeer.com/

We are seeking

We are seeking an experienced Field Application Engineer to lead technical due diligence on data centers for AI and GPU infrastructure deployment. This role is responsible for assessing site readiness, validating usable power and cooling capacity, quantifying gaps and remediation needs, and delivering clear go or no-go recommendations that move qualified sites to deployment. The ideal candidate is a hands-on, detail-driven engineer and clear communicator who thrives in a fast-growing, dynamic environment.

This is a full-time role based in San Jose, CA, with regular travel for on-site assessments and deployment support.

What You Will Be Responsible For

Lead remote reviews and on-site inspections of data centers to determine whether they can support target GPU cluster configurations, capacity, and deployment schedules.
Validate operator claims against drawings, equipment specifications, operating records, utility documentation, and commissioning evidence.
Distinguish utility supply, total facility load, and usable IT capacity, and assess available and committed capacity, rack density, and expansion constraints.
Evaluate power distribution, UPS, backup generation, and redundancy against the needs of high-density AI workloads.
Assess air cooling and direct-to-chip liquid cooling, including heat rejection, cooling distribution units (CDUs), facility water conditions, flow and temperature, piping, and leak detection.
Review rack space, floor loading, delivery access, cabling, carrier diversity, fiber routes, bandwidth, and latency, and partner with network engineering on Ethernet and InfiniBand cluster designs.
Review monitoring, maintenance, incident response, remote hands, physical security, and commissioning and acceptance records to identify operational and resilience gaps.
Classify sites as ready for deployment, requiring defined upgrades, or requiring substantial development.
Produce decision-ready assessments documenting achievable IT capacity, rack count, dependencies, cost estimates, schedule risks, and a go or no-go recommendation.
Resolve technical questions with operators, landlords, utilities, equipment vendors, and contractors.
Define remediation and acceptance criteria, verify closure of critical issues, and hand development work to the appropriate team.
Partner with AI ecosystem, cloud infrastructure, procurement, and engineering teams to build a consistent assessment process and a prioritized pipeline of qualified sites.

How You Will Stand Out

Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a related discipline, or equivalent practical experience.
5+ years of experience in data center engineering, critical facilities, infrastructure solutions engineering, commissioning, or field applications engineering.
Hands-on experience assessing or delivering data centers, with a track record of identifying deployment blockers and driving technical issues to resolution.
Strong working knowledge of electrical and mechanical infrastructure, including power distribution, backup systems, cooling, and the relationship between facility capacity and usable IT load.
Ability to read electrical single-line diagrams, mechanical schematics, equipment data sheets, rack layouts, and commissioning reports.
Understanding of AI or HPC infrastructure requirements, including high-density GPU systems, liquid cooling, and high-speed networking.
Ability to write clear site assessment reports, compare options, estimate remediation scope, and explain technical risks and tradeoffs to business stakeholders.
Strong professional English communication skills and willingness to travel for site assessments and deployment support.
Preferred: experience with GPU cloud, colocation, hyperscale, or HPC facilities, including high-density or liquid-cooled deployments.
Preferred: experience with facility commissioning, integrated systems testing, capacity planning, or converting existing facilities for AI workloads.
Preferred: familiarity with colocation agreements, service-level commitments, utility tariffs, power usage effectiveness (PUE), and total cost of ownership (TCO).
Preferred: experience coordinating equipment vendors, data center operators, and engineering contractors across regions.

What You Will Experience Working With Us

A culture that values authenticity and diverse perspectives.
An inclusive, respectful environment with open workspaces and an energetic, start-up spirit.
A fast-growing company with opportunities to network with industry pioneers and enthusiasts.
The ability to contribute directly and make an impact on the future of the digital asset and AI computing industry.
Involvement in new projects and in developing processes/systems.
Personal accountability, autonomy, rapid growth, and learning opportunities.
Attractive benefits and development such as training and mentoring.

jobs.title: Solutions Architect
jobs.description:
About Us

Lirvana Labs builds Mission Control, an AI system for school leadership. School and district leaders today spend hundreds of hours a year pulling data out of disconnected systems by hand just to answer basic questions: is this intervention working, which students are slipping, what do we tell the board. Mission Control answers those questions in real time. Yeti Confetti Kids, our teaching and learning product, is an AI co-pilot for early numeracy and literacy, covering 200+ skills mapped to Common Core, CASEL, and Bloom’s, and giving educators a clear picture of each child’s cognitive, social, and emotional development.

Everything we ship is co-designed with the partners who will use it: NYC Public Schools, the Urban Assembly, TNTP, the Hong Kong Education Bureau, and the Joan Ganz Cooney Center at Sesame Workshop. That approach has earned recognition from MIT Solve, EdTech Week NYC, IEI (Superintendent’s Choice), and H&K EdCity, but the recognition that matters most is a principal, superintendents, and leaders telling us the product changed how they run their organization.

We started in 2021 and are backed by impact-focused investors: Kapor Capital, Transcend Capital Partners, and Chingona Ventures. We’re headquartered in Silicon Valley with global offices in New York, Singapore, and Hong Kong.

The Role

At the heart of our approach is our co-design process. Every conversation is an opportunity to build a long partnership focused on student impact and system wide change. Today, when a district tells us what they need, the path from that conversation to a working solution runs through several people. We want one person who owns it end-to-end.

You’ll sit in discovery with principals and school leaders, figure out what they actually need (often not what they first ask for), and then build it, which includes prototypes, agentic workflows, evaluations, and data pipelines on top of our platform. Then you carry it through to production and hand it off cleanly for our platform team to maintain. A working prototype closes deals here and builds trust with partners, so you’ll co-own the pipeline with Sales.

Roughly how your time breaks down:

Half building. Prototypes, POCs, custom agentic tools and eval scripts. You own them from design through deployment and handoff.
A quarter in discovery. Running customer conversations alongside Sales and earning technical credibility and trust with partners with your knowledge around our solutions and architecture
A quarter of requirements. Turning what you heard into something shippable, scoping custom workflows, and calling what fits on our platform and what doesn’t and working with our platform and product team on roadmap dependencies.

You report to the Head of Product and work day to day with Sales, Engineering, and DevOps.

What This Looks Like In Practice

A few examples of the kind of work you’d own:

A district wants to know which 9th graders are at risk of not graduating, but their attendance, grades, and behavior data live in three systems that have never talked to each other. You design the pipeline, build the early-warning logic on Mission Control, and sit with their data lead until it’s running on their real data.
A school network wants an agent that drafts comprehensive education plans from a student’s recent data. You scope it with the principal, build a working version, run evals against what their team would have written, and iterate until it’s good enough to put in front of staff

How We Work

Small team, high ownership, biased toward action. We co-design and build with partners, show them unfinished prototypes, and change course when we learn something. Nobody will manage you closely; you’ll be trusted to make calls and expected to own the outcomes.

The mission is the reason most of us are here. The people on the other end of this work are school leaders responsible for thousands of students, and the students themselves, many of them multilingual learners in under-resourced schools. The work is hard and the systems are old and the data is a mess, and when it works, a kid who was going to fall through the cracks doesn’t. We take that seriously.

Why this role, specifically

You’ll own the full arc from first conversation to production, which almost no role at a larger company lets you do.
You’ll build agentic systems on real data for real users, not demos.
Your work will directly shape the roadmap. When you find a gap, you’re in the room deciding whether we fill it.
You’ll get paid on the deals you help close, on top of base and equity.

What We’re Looking For

4+ years shipping production software, including time as the technical person in the room with customers.
You can take a user story from a non-technical stakeholder, turn it into something buildable, and build it yourself. You’re comfortable owning code in production.
Snowflake and modern data engineering: pipelines, ETL, data modeling, SQL optimization. School data is messy and you’ve worked with messy data before.
You’ve built n8n workflows and know how agentic workflows plug into a data stack.
You’ve sold, or been close to the sale: multiple stakeholders, objection handling, keeping a deal moving with leadership on the other side.
You can run a project end to end and keep the timeline honest.
You make day-to-day technical calls without asking permission, and you have the judgment to make them well.
You explain technical things plainly. Superintendents and principals are time strapped leaders and you need to get to the point.
You’ve led a small team or mentored junior full-stack engineers.
You’d rather ship a scoped version than polish a slide.

Nice to have:
forward-deployed engineering experience, or you’ve started something or been early at something.

Next Steps

Ready to apply? We’d love to hear from you. Please record a 2-minute video covering the following and send the link with your application.

Would you rather go and speak with a customer directly by yourself, or work together with the sales and product team? Why?
Talk about an entrepreneurial experience
What would make you quit?

This exercise is very important and is the first step in the evaluation process.

Our Hiring Philosophy

We know that the "perfect" candidate doesn't exist, and that skills can be learned. We're more interested in your passion for this work, your potential, and what you can add to our team. If you believe you have what it takes, but don't meet every single bullet point, please apply anyway!

jobs.title: ML Silicon Performance Lead
jobs.description:
About The Team

OpenAI’s Hardware organization develops AI-native silicon and system-level solutions for the unique demands of advanced AI workloads. Building on efforts like Jalapeño, the team is developing future generations of AI-native silicon and tightly integrated systems to power the next generation of frontier models. By co-designing chips, systems, tools, and methodologies, the team helps deliver faster, more efficient, and production-ready hardware for OpenAI’s supercomputing platform.

About The Role

We’re looking for an ML Silicon Performance Lead to drive hardware/software co-design for our silicon architecture. You will work across models, kernels, compilers, and silicon to shape how ML workloads map to hardware—and how the hardware should evolve to support them. Your work will connect model and workload requirements with compute, memory, and specialized acceleration capabilities to maximize performance, efficiency, and scalability across current and future generations of AI silicon.

You’ll partner closely with ML research, compiler, and silicon architecture teams to jointly develop software approaches and hardware capabilities. From kernel mapping and quantization to new data structures and specialized IP, you’ll evaluate hardware and software tradeoffs to improve performance, efficiency, and utilization across large-scale AI workloads. Through performance modeling, simulation, and hands-on optimization, you’ll guide architectural decisions and validate improvements on representative workloads.

In This Role, You Will

Drive hardware/software co-design across ML research, compiler, and silicon teams, jointly shaping kernel implementations and hardware capabilities to meet workload performance and efficiency goals.
Partner with ML research to translate model and workload needs into kernel performance targets and compute, memory capacity, and bandwidth requirements, feeding hardware constraints and opportunities back into model and algorithm choices.
Map and optimize ML kernels for architecture, using insights from data movement, memory hierarchy, and execution efficiency to guide both software improvements and hardware design.
Co-design support for new data structures and quantization formats across kernels, compilers, and silicon, balancing model quality, numerical behavior, performance, power, and implementation cost.
Define and help develop specialized acceleration IP, working with compiler and silicon partners to determine the right division of functionality across software, instructions, and dedicated hardware.
Drive ML performance modeling and simulation with the compiler team to compare hardware/software design options, expose bottlenecks, and quantify end-to-end benefits on representative workloads.
Partner with the Silicon Architecture lead and silicon team to specify and validate new IP, using kernel and simulation results to refine requirements and prioritize architectural improvements.

You Might Thrive In This Role If You

Have deep experience with ML accelerator architecture and how compute resources, memory systems, and data movement shape workload performance.
Can translate model-level behavior into concrete kernel requirements and hardware design decisions.
Have built or used accelerator performance models and simulators, and know how to validate their assumptions and interpret their limitations.
Have hands-on experience optimizing ML kernels, including identifying bottlenecks and improving utilization, locality, and execution efficiency.
Understand quantization and numerical formats, including their implications for model quality, memory bandwidth, compute efficiency, and hardware support.
Have experience with hardware/software co-design and can reason about whether a capability belongs in a kernel, compiler, instruction set, or dedicated hardware.
Work effectively across research, compiler, and silicon teams, bringing clarity to ambiguous requirements and building alignment through technical evidence.

To comply with U.S. export control laws and regulations, candidates for this role may need to meet certain legal status requirements as provided in those laws and regulations.

About OpenAI

OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company dedicated to ensuring that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products. AI is an extremely powerful tool that must be created with safety and human needs at its core, and to achieve our mission, we must encompass and value the many different perspectives, voices, and experiences that form the full spectrum of humanity.

We are an equal opportunity employer, and we do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, age, veteran status, disability, genetic information, or other applicable legally protected characteristic.

For additional information, please see OpenAI’s Affirmative Action and Equal Employment Opportunity Policy Statement.

In addition, job duties require access to secure and protected information technology systems and related data security obligations.

jobs.description:
About Rippling

Rippling gives businesses one place to run HR, IT, and Finance. It brings together all of the workforce systems that are normally scattered across a company, like payroll, expenses, benefits, and computers. For the first time ever, you can manage and automate every part of the employee lifecycle in a single system.

Take onboarding, for example. With Rippling, you can hire a new employee anywhere in the world and set up their payroll, corporate card, computer, benefits, and even third-party apps like Slack and Microsoft 365—all within 90 seconds.

Based in San Francisco, CA, Rippling has raised $1.4B+ from the world’s top investors—including Kleiner Perkins, Founders Fund, Sequoia, Greenoaks, and Bedrock—and was named one of America's best startup employers by Forbes.

We prioritize candidate safety. Please be aware that all official communication will only be sent from @Rippling.com addresses.

About The Role

At Rippling, we are not just building AI features, we are building an autonomous operating system for work. We are investing heavily in the next generation of enterprise AI: intelligent background automation, systems that monitor and improve themselves, and a custom intelligence layer built on Rippling's unique data and workflows.

The opportunity is to push the boundaries of what machine learning can do in the enterprise through purpose-built ML systems that learn from Rippling's proprietary data graph to deliver compounding intelligence across every product surface. You will be joining the team that recently launched Rippling AI, the fastest-growing product in Rippling's history. The models and ML systems you build will be the intelligence powering every AI surface at Rippling.

As a Senior Machine Learning Engineer, you will own the end-to-end ML lifecycle for projects within the AI Cloud team: problem formulation, data preparation, model development, evaluation, and production deployment. You will partner with Staff engineers and cross-functional teammates to make Rippling's agents reliable, accurate, and continuously improving. This is a deeply hands-on role, with opportunities to lead project-level technical decisions and contribute to the team's broader ML direction.

What You Will Do

Own the end-to-end machine learning lifecycle for high-impact AI projects, from problem definition through production deployment and iteration.
Design and implement ML systems—including fine-tuned LLMs, RAG, reward models, and multi-agent orchestration—tailored to Rippling's enterprise domain.
Build robust evaluation and experimentation capabilities: offline benchmarks, A/B testing, and continuous monitoring of model quality.
Develop training pipelines and data flywheels that leverage Rippling's structured data graph.
Take ML techniques from research to production: evaluate where RLHF, distillation, structured decoding, and tool-use training can improve model quality, reliability, and efficiency.
Build and improve feedback loops, active learning workflows, and automated retraining pipelines.
Partner closely with Product and Platform teams to translate requirements into reliable ML systems and deliver measurable product improvements.
Contribute to design and code reviews, share ML best practices, and mentor engineers within the team.
Stay current with ML research and apply relevant advances to production systems.

What You Will Need

5+ years of software engineering experience, including 3+ years focused on ML, with experience shipping and operating ML systems in production.
Strong practical experience with modern ML, including LLMs, transformer architectures, fine-tuning, and RAG; familiarity with RLHF or related model-alignment techniques.
Strong fundamentals in classical ML and statistics.
Hands-on proficiency with ML frameworks such as PyTorch or JAX and production ML infrastructure.
Experience building evaluation systems for generative AI.
Demonstrated ability to independently deliver complex ML projects, make sound technical tradeoffs, and collaborate across functions.
Strong product instincts and an ability to connect model improvements to customer outcomes.
Clear, precise communication to diverse audiences.
Comfort with ambiguity and high velocity.
Publications in top ML venues (NeurIPS, ICML, ACL, EMNLP) are a plus.
Experience with enterprise data or knowledge graphs is a plus.

Additional Information

Rippling is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to building a diverse and inclusive workforce and do not discriminate based on race, religion, color, national origin, ancestry, physical disability, mental disability, medical condition, genetic information, marital status, sex, gender, gender identity, gender expression, age, sexual orientation, veteran or military status, or any other legally protected characteristics, Rippling is committed to providing reasonable accommodations for candidates with disabilities who need assistance during the hiring process. To request a reasonable accommodation, please email accommodations@rippling.com

Rippling highly values having employees working in-office to foster a collaborative work environment and company culture. For office-based employees (employees who live within a defined radius of a Rippling office), Rippling considers working in the office, at least three days a week under current policy, to be an essential function of the employee's role.

jobs.title: ML Data Infrastructure Engineer
jobs.description:
Are you ready to revolutionize the advertising industry?

At Cognitiv, we are not just another AdTech company—we are industry trailblazers redefining media buying with our Deep Learning Advertising Platform. Since 2015, we have harnessed the power of cutting-edge deep learning technology and data science to transform how brands connect with their customers. Our mission? To bring intelligence to advertising and deliver unparalleled precision, relevance, and impact at scale.

With our innovative platform, advertisers enjoy unprecedented flexibility—whether it is activating Dynamic Deals through their preferred DSP, leveraging our managed service DSP, or utilizing our industry-first ContextGPT product. As a part of Cognitiv, you will be at the forefront of AI-driven advertising solutions, driving change and achieving remarkable growth in a rapidly evolving industry.

Now, we’re growing!

In this role, you will work at the intersection of large-scale distributed systems, machine learning engineering, and platform architecture. You will own and evolve critical data capabilities within Cognitiv’s advertising ecosystem, with a primary focus on designing and delivering stable, highly scalable feature pipelines, as well as optimizing the performance and reliability of ad model training pipelines.

This is a senior individual-contributor role for an engineer who thrives on solving complex platform problems, raising the technical bar, and building systems that serve many teams at scale. You will partner closely with engineers, product managers, data scientists, infrastructure teams, and downstream data consumers to deliver platforms that are resilient, extensible, and easy to adopt.

This position will be located in San Mateo, CA with a hybrid work schedule of 3 days in office (Mon/Tue/Wed) and 2 days remote optional (Thursday/Friday).

What You'll Do

High-Performance Feature Engineering & Infrastructure: Architect, build, and maintain low-latency, high-throughput feature pipelines — batch, real-time streaming, and point-in-time correct historical features — to power our real-time bidding systems.
Advanced Embeddings & Generative AI Integration: Leverage LLMs and deep learning models to extract rich contextual and user-level embeddings into the core feature store/serving system, optimizing embedding generation, indexing, and online retrieval for sub-millisecond serving SLAs.
Model Training Pipeline Optimization: Own and continuously enhance Cognitiv's ad model training pipelines, improving training speed, resource utilization, and throughput for large-scale deep learning models.
System Scalability, Reliability & Efficiency: Establish technical standards for monitoring, testing, and CI/CD across feature and training infrastructure to ensure robust system SLAs/SLOs.
Partner with Modeling & Data Science: Translate complex signals into production-ready features that directly boost model performance (e.g., CTR/CVR prediction).

Who You Are

Must haves:

Strong Fundamentals / First Principles Thinking
3-5+ years of hands-on Machine Learning Infrastructure / Data Platform experience supporting data-intensive platforms, including large-scale data pipelines, streaming systems, and storage layers.
Proficiency in one or more core programming languages — Python, Java, or Scala — for building, maintaining, and scaling robust ML and data pipelines.
Domain expertise in AdTech.
Strong expertise in modern big data technologies such as Apache Spark, Apache Flink, Apache Kafka, and other distributed data processing frameworks.
Excellent team communication, cross-functional collaboration, and problem-solving skills, with a track record of partnering effectively with modeling and engineering teams.

Nice To Haves

Domain expertise in AdTech
Hands-on experience with PyTorch for model architecture, training pipeline acceleration, or distributed training.
Proficiency with cloud & infrastructure technologies, including AWS/GCP, as well as containerization and orchestration platforms like Kubernetes (K8s) and Docker.
Competitive programming background, such as awards or achievements in OI (Olympiad in Informatics) or ACM/ICPC.

Tech Stack:
Python, Java, Kafka, Flink, Spark, PyTorch, Kubernetes, AWS

First 30 Days

What Success Looks Like in Your First 30/60/90 Days

Ramp quickly on Cognitiv's feature pipelines, training infrastructure, and RTB systems.
Build strong context on current architecture, data flows, and known bottlenecks.
Establish relationships with Modeling, Data Science, and Infrastructure teams.
Identify early opportunities to improve pipeline reliability, training efficiency, or serving latency.

First 60 Days

Independently own at least one core feature pipeline, embedding service, or training subsystem.
Ship a first measurable improvement — e.g., reduced serving latency, faster training throughput, or expanded monitoring/CI-CD coverage.
Align with Modeling and Data Science on the feature and training roadmap.
Begin influencing technical direction for feature and training infrastructure.

First 90 Days

Fully own a core area of the platform, such as embedding generation/retrieval, streaming infrastructure, or training pipeline performance.
Deliver measurable business impact — e.g., reduced feature or serving latency, faster model training, or improved uptime/SLA adherence.
Redesign or scale at least one key system to handle growing data volume or model complexity.
Operate autonomously as a trusted technical partner to Modeling, Data Science, and Engineering.

Salary:
$175,000-$225,000 USD Base Salary + Equity

What We Offer

Compensation is based on experience, skills, and other factors. Base salary is just one part of your total rewards at Cognitiv—you’ll also receive equity and a comprehensive benefits package.

Highlights Include

Medical, Dental and Vision plan for US employees & Extended Health Benefits for Canadian employees
12 weeks paid parental leave + 4 weeks WFH
Unlimited PTO + Work-From-Anywhere August
Career development with clear advancement paths
Equity for all employees
Hybrid work model & daily team lunch
Health & wellness stipend + cell phone reimbursement
401(k) & RRSP with employer match
Parking (CA, WA, Vancouver offices) & pre-tax commuter benefits
Employee Assistance Program
Comprehensive onboarding (Cognitiv University)
…and more!

What You’ll Find at Cognitiv

Festiv – We make work fun with cross-team games, events, and creative team bonding.
Responsiv – You’ll be close to clients and leadership, influencing real outcomes.
Inclusiv – Diversity and individuality are celebrated across all levels.
Inventiv – We reward curiosity and embrace bold ideas.
Transformativ – We support your growth with training, mentorship, and flexibility.
Collaborativ – We operate across coasts, connected by purpose and teamwork.

Cognitiv is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive workplace for all.

1162122_RR00119547 Job ID: 1162122_RR00119547

NYU Grossman School of Medicine is one of the nation's top-ranked medical schools. For 175 years, NYU Grossman School of Medicine has trained thousands of physicians and scientists who have helped to shape the course of medical history and enrich the lives of countless people. An integral part of NYU Langone Health, the Grossman School of Medicine at its core is committed to improving the human condition through medical education, scientific research, and direct patient care. At NYU Langone Health, equity and inclusion are fundamental values. We strive to be a place where our exceptionally talented faculty, staff, and students of all identities can thrive. We embrace inclusion and individual skills, ideas, and knowledge.

For more information, go to med.nyu.edu , and interact with us on LinkedIn , Glassdoor , Indeed , Facebook , Twitter and Instagram .

Position Summary

We have an exciting opportunity to join our team as a Data Science Analyst / Engineer.

We are seeking a qualified Data Scientist Analyst to work within the Division of Applied AI Technologies at NYU Langone Health. The individual will be positioned to contribute to analytics efforts at NYU. By teaming up with clinicians, operations, and administrative teams, the individual will develop innovative and impactful data-driven healthcare solutions.

Job Responsibilities

Design and build data solutions using state-of-the-art machine learning and informatics methods.
Work with large, complex, and noisy clinical datasets to solve challenging problems in the healthcare domain.
Build and engineer workflows to collect, store, clean, and process structured and unstructured data, and verify their integrity and appropriateness for specific business processes and analytics systems.
Deploy and integrate these products within the larger ecosystem of healthcare infrastructure at NYULMC.
Prepare and present oral and written results and reports to a variety of audiences regarding processes, models, evaluation, and impact (ROI).
Lead high-priority data-oriented projects, including development, deployment, and evaluation.
Collaborate with associate data scientists, engineers, and clinically trained professionals to test novel approaches and support the implementation, maintenance, and improvement of predictive models.
Collaborate with the broader NYULMC healthcare community and contribute to ongoing predictive modeling and analytics efforts.
Establish key metrics, run experiments, and perform analyses to understand the incremental impact of efforts to drive adoption and engagement.
Contribute to data science best practices and mentor team members to elevate the technical capabilities and impact of the group.
Quantify the impact of model improvements and communicate trade-offs to stakeholders.
Build evaluation frameworks, validate model behavior prospectively and silently, and oversee ongoing maintenance.
Design systems, infrastructure, abstractions, and processes that accelerate development time for future projects.
Manage and plan go-live activities and define the necessary steps to ensure timely delivery.
Balance perfection with production readiness, iterate quickly, and recognize when a minimum viable product outperforms a six-month research project.
Contribute ideas and innovations to solve internal and stakeholder problems.

experience in machine learning/ data science.

Knowledge of predictive modeling and machine learning concepts, including design,

development, evaluation, deployment and scaling to large datasets

Good grasp of soware engineering principles. Experience in integrating modern

software architectures.

Knowledge and some experience in operational aspects of soware development and

deployment, including automation, testing, virtualization and container technology

Excellent written and oral communication skills for a variety of audiences

PhD degree in a quantitative field (Biomedical Informatics, Computer Science, Machine

Learning, Applied Stascs, Mathematics or similar field) + 2 years experience.

Demonstrated skills in design and implementation of complex machine learning models.

Demonstrated knowledge of soware engineering and operational skills through prior

projects.

jobs.title: Forward Deployed Software Engineer, Connected Warfare (Active Clearance)
jobs.description:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

About The Team

The Connected Warfare division’s Mission Command team builds, deploys, integrates, extends, and scales Anduril's software and hardware to deliver mission-critical capabilities to our customers. As the software engineers closest to Anduril customers and end-users, Mission Software Engineers solve technical challenges of operational scenarios while owning the end-to-end delivery of winning capabilities such as Lattice Mesh, Joint All Domain Command & Control, and Anduril's Menace Family-of-Systems.

As a Software Engineer on the Mission Command team, you will build the foundation for a first-of-its-kind platform designed for the tactical edge, solving novel problems across networking, autonomy, systems integration, robotics, and next-generation distributed data layers. Powering resilient, machine-speed decision-making for warfighters and allies—even in contested, disconnected environments—your work will ensure Anduril’s products seamlessly work together and with third parties to deliver customer value. Driven by a “Whatever It Takes” mindset, the Mission Command team balances intentional, long-term system design with the pragmatic tradeoffs needed to meet immediate customer needs. By keeping the mission top-of-mind, you will make sound, scalable engineering decisions to deliver high-quality, expedient software that preemptively addresses the national security challenges of the future.

What You’ll Do

Own software solutions spanning core mesh platforms, data interfaces, and release management deployed directly to customers to scale critical mission capabilities.
Deliver well-architected systems using modern software engineering practices—including code and design reviews—while championing scalability, reliability, testability, portability, and maintainability.
Drive software solutions end-to-end, partnering closely with end-users to translate complex needs into features while balancing user experience with engineering constraints.
Collaborate across multiple teams to plan, build, and test complex, cross-functional functionality.
Ensure system health and rapid resolution by creating and analyzing monitoring metrics, triaging production issues, root-causing failures, and coordinating next steps.
Travel 10% – 30% of the time to meet customers wherever in the world they are, collaborate with teammates across the globe, understand real-world operating conditions, and build, test, and deploy capabilities directly in the field.

Required Qualifications

Currently possesses and is able to maintain an active U.S. Secret Clearance
Strong engineering background from industry or school, ideally in areas/fields such as Computer Science, Software Engineering, Networking, Mathematics, or Physics
At least 3-10+ years working with a variety of programming languages such as Go, Python, Java, C++, Rust, etc.
Experience building software solutions involving significant amounts of data processing and analysis
Ability to quickly understand and navigate complex systems and established code bases
A desire to work on critical software that has a real-world impact

Preferred Qualifications

Experience working with and designing distributed systems
Proven ability to deliver high-quality results at pace, ideally within a startup or high-growth environment
Deep networking experience, especially for distributed systems operating in non-standard networking conditions
Familiarity with industry standard cloud platforms (AWS, Azure) and software infrastructure fundamentals (networking, security, distributed systems)
A deep, demonstrated understanding of how computers and networks work, from a single desktop to a multi-cluster cloud node
Professional software development lifecycle experience using tools such as version control, CICD systems, etc.
Familiarity with industry standard monitoring, logging, and data management tools and best practices

US Salary Range

$114,000—$192,000 USD

Benefits

The salary range for this role is an estimate based on a wide range of compensation factors, inclusive of base salary only. Actual salary offer may vary based on (but not limited to) work experience, education and/or training, critical skills, and/or business considerations. Highly competitive equity grants are included in the majority of full time offers; and are considered part of Anduril's total compensation package. Additionally, Anduril offers top-tier benefits for full-time employees, including:

At Anduril, we invest in our people. Our comprehensive, competitive benefits package (available at little to no cost to employees) ensures you’re supported in health, recovery, and whatever comes next. For more information, Explore Our Benefits.

Protecting Yourself from Recruitment Scams

Anduril is committed to maintaining the integrity of our Talent acquisition process and the security of our candidates. We've observed a rise in sophisticated phishing and fraudulent schemes where individuals impersonate Anduril representatives, luring job seekers with false interviews or job offers. These scammers often attempt to extract payment or sensitive personal information.

To Ensure Your Safety And Help You Navigate Your Job Search With Confidence, Please Keep The Following Critical Points In Mind

No Financial Requests: Anduril will never solicit payment or demand personal financial details (such as banking information, credit card numbers, or social security numbers) at any stage of our hiring process. Our legitimate recruitment is entirely free for candidates.
Please always verify communications:
Direct from Anduril: If you receive an email from one of our recruiters, it will only come from an @anduril.com address.
Via Agency Partner: If contacted by a recruiting agency for an Anduril role, their email will clearly identify their agency. If you suspect any suspicious activity, please verify the agency's authenticity by reaching out to contact@anduril.com.

Exercise Caution with Unsolicited Outreach: If you receive any communication that appears suspicious, contains grammatical errors, or makes unusual requests, do not engage. Always confirm the sender's email domain is @anduril.com before providing any personal information or clicking on links.
What to Do If You Suspect Fraud: Should you encounter any questionable or fraudulent outreach claiming to be from Anduril, please report it immediately to contact@anduril.com. Your proactive caution is invaluable in protecting your personal information and upholding the security and trustworthiness of our recruitment efforts.

Data Privacy

To view Anduril's candidate data privacy policy, please visit https://anduril.com/applicant-privacy-notice/.

By submitting your application, you consent to Anduril Industries using a third-party service provider to conduct pre-employment risk, integrity, and due diligence screening and assessing potential risks as part of your application process. jobs.description:
About Rippling

Rippling gives businesses one place to run HR, IT, and Finance. It brings together all of the workforce systems that are normally scattered across a company, like payroll, expenses, benefits, and computers. For the first time ever, you can manage and automate every part of the employee lifecycle in a single system.

Take onboarding, for example. With Rippling, you can hire a new employee anywhere in the world and set up their payroll, corporate card, computer, benefits, and even third-party apps like Slack and Microsoft 365—all within 90 seconds.

Based in San Francisco, CA, Rippling has raised $1.4B+ from the world’s top investors—including Kleiner Perkins, Founders Fund, Sequoia, Greenoaks, and Bedrock—and was named one of America's best startup employers by Forbes.

We prioritize candidate safety. Please be aware that all official communication will only be sent from @Rippling.com addresses.

About The Role

At Rippling, we are not just building AI features, we are building an autonomous operating system for work. We are investing heavily in the next generation of enterprise AI: intelligent background automation, systems that monitor and improve themselves, and a custom intelligence layer built on Rippling's unique data and workflows.

The opportunity is to push the boundaries of what machine learning can do in the enterprise through purpose-built ML systems that learn from Rippling's proprietary data graph to deliver compounding intelligence across every product surface. You will be joining the team that recently launched Rippling AI, the fastest-growing product in Rippling's history. The models and ML systems you build will be the intelligence powering every AI surface at Rippling.

As a Senior Machine Learning Engineer, you will own the end-to-end ML lifecycle for projects within the AI Cloud team: problem formulation, data preparation, model development, evaluation, and production deployment. You will partner with Staff engineers and cross-functional teammates to make Rippling's agents reliable, accurate, and continuously improving. This is a deeply hands-on role, with opportunities to lead project-level technical decisions and contribute to the team's broader ML direction.

What You Will Do

Own the end-to-end machine learning lifecycle for high-impact AI projects, from problem definition through production deployment and iteration.
Design and implement ML systems—including fine-tuned LLMs, RAG, reward models, and multi-agent orchestration—tailored to Rippling's enterprise domain.
Build robust evaluation and experimentation capabilities: offline benchmarks, A/B testing, and continuous monitoring of model quality.
Develop training pipelines and data flywheels that leverage Rippling's structured data graph.
Take ML techniques from research to production: evaluate where RLHF, distillation, structured decoding, and tool-use training can improve model quality, reliability, and efficiency.
Build and improve feedback loops, active learning workflows, and automated retraining pipelines.
Partner closely with Product and Platform teams to translate requirements into reliable ML systems and deliver measurable product improvements.
Contribute to design and code reviews, share ML best practices, and mentor engineers within the team.
Stay current with ML research and apply relevant advances to production systems.

What You Will Need

5+ years of software engineering experience, including 3+ years focused on ML, with experience shipping and operating ML systems in production.
Strong practical experience with modern ML, including LLMs, transformer architectures, fine-tuning, and RAG; familiarity with RLHF or related model-alignment techniques.
Strong fundamentals in classical ML and statistics.
Hands-on proficiency with ML frameworks such as PyTorch or JAX and production ML infrastructure.
Experience building evaluation systems for generative AI.
Demonstrated ability to independently deliver complex ML projects, make sound technical tradeoffs, and collaborate across functions.
Strong product instincts and an ability to connect model improvements to customer outcomes.
Clear, precise communication to diverse audiences.
Comfort with ambiguity and high velocity.
Publications in top ML venues (NeurIPS, ICML, ACL, EMNLP) are a plus.
Experience with enterprise data or knowledge graphs is a plus.

jobs.description:
How you move is why we’re here. ®

Now more than ever.

Get back to what you need and love to do.

The possibilities are endless...

Now more than ever, our guiding principles are helping us in our search for exceptional talent - candidates who align with our unique workplace culture and who want to maximize the abundant opportunities for growth and success.

If this describes you then let’s talk!

HSS is consistently among the top-ranked hospitals for orthopedics and rheumatology by U.S. News & World Report. As a recipient of the Magnet Award for Nursing Excellence, HSS was the first hospital in New York City to receive the distinguished designation. Whether you are early in your career or an expert in your field, you will find HSS an innovative, supportive and inclusive environment.

Working with colleagues who love what they do and are deeply committed to our Mission, you too can be part of our transformation across the enterprise.

Emp Status

Regular Full time

Work Shift

Day (United States of America)

Compensation Range

The base pay scale for this position is $101,500.00 - $172,500.00. In addition, this position will be eligible for additional benefits consistent with the role. The salary of the finalist selected for this role will be determined based on various factors, including but not limited to: scope of role, level of experience, education, accomplishments, internal equity, budget, and subject to Fair Market Value evaluation. The hiring range listed is a good faith determination of potential compensation at the time of this job advertisement and may be modified in the future.

What You Will Be Doing

What you’ll do

Find and frame the right problems. Work with domain experts to identify opportunities, including needs that were never articulated as “data-science requests”. Turn vague questions — “what will demand look like next quarter?”, “why are cases running late?”, or “did this intervention actually help?” — into well-posed problems with explicit assumptions, a decision or workflow they will change, and a credible way to measure impact and value.
Build data-science-driven products, not artifacts. Deliver advanced analytics and data-science-driven features through applications and real products (not stand-alone notebooks) that clinicians, operators, researchers, finance teams, and executives can rely on and keep using. Own or contribute across design, prototyping, development, testing, deployment, integration, monitoring, and iteration.
Use the right analytical method for the decision. Apply predictive modeling and forecasting, experimentation and A/B testing, causal or program-effectiveness analysis, segmentation, anomaly detection, risk stratification, and novel measurement where each is appropriate. Challenge weak designs, quantify uncertainty, and know when a simpler method is the better answer.
Personally productionize the work. Write maintainable code, integrate models and analytical logic into applications and Databricks workflows, create appropriate evaluation and monitoring, respond to drift or failure, and keep improving the product after launch. We do not throw a notebook over the wall and call the work finished.
Build reusable capability. Improve shared approaches for rapid model development, feature and evaluation pipelines, model cards, monitoring, documentation, and reproducibility. Recognize when a method, dataset, feature, or workflow built in one domain can solve a problem elsewhere.
Work in “garages”. Build collaboratively with domain experts at the hip during daily, synchronous working sessions. Push back, ask questions, change course on new evidence, and explain complex quantitative ideas clearly to clinical, operational, research, finance, and executive audiences.
Work with AI fluently, but skeptically. Use agentic coding tooling to move fast, with the judgment to know what to delegate and what to think hard on, and the instinct to catch quiet mistakes and implicit assumptions that should be challenged.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in a quantitative field (e.g., data science, statistics, computer science, engineering, applied math, economics, operations research, or similar), or equivalent demonstrated technical ability.
Master’s or above is preferred but not required for Data Scientist II roles. For all roles, we weigh demonstrated ability over credentials.

Strong data science, statistics, and modeling foundations. The ability to explain and defend modeling and design choices, understand the methods you invoke, spot leakage and confounding, quantify uncertainty, and insist on performance metrics tailored to the problem at hand.
Strong programming ability and experience (e.g., Python, SQL). Comfort working with git, building within applications, and working in a cloud/lakehouse environment; we use Databricks and AWS.
Prior Databricks experience is preferred.

Prior experience working on projects involving large datasets, including the design, prototyping, development, testing, deployment, and monitoring of statistical and machine learning models. Specific experience building data-science-driven features, progressing work from problem ideation and formulation to live app-based product features or decision-support tools that users really used, were monitored, and were iterated on is ideal.
Data Scientist I: Generally 0-2 years of professional data science or advanced analytics experience. Strong graduate, internship, fellowship, research, or substantial applied-project work can count. DS I candidates should have exposure to end-to-end production experience or must be ready to learn this quickly.
Data Scientist II: Generally 3-5+ years of professional data science or advanced analytics experience, with a record of independently leading work from problem discovery and formulation through deployment, application integration, monitoring, and iteration. DS II candidates must already have substantial end-to-end production experience.
Experience in one or more of forecasting, experimentation, causal inference, anomaly detection, risk stratification, optimization, or measurement design.
Experience with healthcare data, in a US-based healthcare delivery or health-tech setting, especially in musculoskeletal health and orthopedics, is preferred. Other useful domain backgrounds may include operations, finance, economics, research, clinical science, consumer or digital products, or other complex enterprise settings.

Strong experience with modern AI agentic coding tools and techniques. Robust skepticism and the judgment to discern what tasks are best left to AI and what tasks are fundamentally human (framing objectives and goals, verifying work aligns with those). The ability and curiosity to keep up on the latest models, their strengths and weaknesses, and effective strategies for using them.
High intelligence and ability to frame messy problems into structured ones, including exercising judgment about assumptions and unknowns, and what actually matters for a given problem (things that AI cannot do for us).
Flexibility, communication, collaboration, comfort with ambiguity, and the ability to leverage those skills to ramp up quickly in a new environment, work well with domain experts who are not data experts, translate complex concepts for those audiences without being steamrolled, and course correct with new information.
Drive and vision with a bias toward action and ownership. Having a point of view about where things should go, not just how to execute a direct ask or ticket. DS II candidates particularly should be able to operate autonomously, lead through influence rather than authority, juggle competing priorities, mentor others, and connect work across domains.

Non-Discrimination Policy

Hospital for Special Surgery is committed to providing high quality care and skilled, compassionate, reliable service to our community in a safe and healing environment. Consistent with this commitment, Hospital for Special Surgery provides care, admits, and treats patients and provides all services without regard to age, race, color, creed, ethnicity, religion, national origin, culture, language, physical or mental disability, socioeconomic status, veteran or military status, marital status, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other basis prohibited by federal, state, or local law or by accreditation standards.

to join our Digital Advisory team at our New York City, NY or Boston, MA offices. Working under the guidance of senior engineers and solution architects, you will help deliver AI agents, copilots, workflow automations, and data-driven applications that support clients across the Architecture, Engineering, and Construction (AEC) industry.

You will work directly with clients to understand business requirements, demonstrate solutions, troubleshoot issues, and translate technical concepts into clear, actionable outcomes. Success in this role requires technical curiosity, strong communication skills, professionalism in client settings, and a desire to continuously learn emerging AI technologies.

Key Responsibilities

AI Solution Development

Build, configure, test, and support AI agents, copilots, and intelligent workflows using Microsoft Copilot Studio, Azure AI Foundry, Power Platform, and Power Automate.
Assist in the development and deployment of AI-driven solutions that solve operational, business, and project delivery challenges.
Participate in solution design sessions and contribute ideas for improving performance, usability, and scalability.
Support the integration of AI capabilities into existing client platforms and business processes.
Develop and maintain prompts, knowledge sources, workflows, and agent configurations following established standards and best practices.

Participate in client-facing workshops, discovery sessions, and solution demonstrations.
Gather business and technical requirements directly from stakeholders and document findings.
Explain AI concepts, technical solutions, and implementation approaches in language accessible to non-technical audiences.
Troubleshoot issues during demonstrations, testing, and production deployments while maintaining professionalism and composure.
Support onsite client engagements as required throughout the project lifecycle.

Data & Platform Engineering

Develop and maintain data flows across Microsoft platforms including Dataverse, Microsoft Fabric, OneLake, SharePoint, and Microsoft 365.
Assist with data preparation, transformation, integration, and governance activities supporting AI solutions.
Support secure and scalable data architectures that enable effective AI and automation capabilities.
Collaborate with software engineers, data engineers, and architects to ensure successful solution delivery.

Engineering Excellence

Write clean, maintainable, and well-documented code and configurations.
Participate in code reviews, testing activities, and quality assurance processes.
Follow established development standards, naming conventions, security practices, and documentation requirements.
Contribute to technical documentation, deployment guides, runbooks, user guides, and knowledge-sharing materials.

Professional Growth & Project Ownership

jobs.description:
About Checkr

Checkr is building the data platform to power safe and fair decisions. Over 140,000 companies and millions of people rely on Checkr for AI verification in the moments that matter most: getting a new job, a new place to live, a car ride, childcare, even a date. Customers include Uber, Pennymac, Airbnb, Doordash, and Anthropic.

We’re a team that thrives on solving complex problems with innovative solutions that advance our mission. Checkr is recognized on Forbes Cloud 100 2025 List and is a Y Combinator 2024 Breakthrough Company.

About The Team/role

We’re hiring an ML Engineer (P3) to build and ship the AI systems that power Checkr’s core products. This role sits on the ML team inside Checkr’s Data & ML organization within Engineering.

Checkr runs millions of background checks a year. The ML team builds the systems that make those checks faster, more accurate, and cheaper to operate: document processing, charge classification, entity resolution, and in-product intelligence. These are production services that Product Engineering depends on daily.

This is not a research role or a notebook role. You’ll own ML services end-to-end: design them, code them, deploy them, monitor them. We need someone who writes production software, builds with LLMs and APIs as first-class tools, and can tell the difference between working code and AI slop. If you’ve spent the last few years building AI-native software and you care deeply about engineering craft, we want to talk.

This role sits in the central Data & ML team within the Engineering organization. You will partner daily with Product Engineering, Product, and cross-functional teams. You’ll also contribute to Checkr’s broader AI strategy, including our initiative to deploy our agentic fleet and build scalable context with our semantic layer.

We are looking for someone based in San Francisco who has built ML systems in fast-moving, impact-first environments. Less process, more shipping. Less paperwork, more results.

What You’ll Do

Build and deploy ML/AI services. Design, develop, and ship ML models and AI systems that Product Engineering teams rely on. You write the model code, the API layer, the monitoring, and the tests. Not notebooks; production services.
Design with LLMs and APIs. Use LLM APIs (OpenAI, Anthropic, etc.) as building blocks in production systems. You know when to call an LLM, when to fine-tune, when to use a classical model, and when to write a rule. You think about cost, latency, and quality together.
Ship production software. Write clean, well-structured code with solid OOP, proper abstractions, error handling, and tests. Your code gets reviewed by SWEs and passes. CI/CD is how you work, not something you bolt on at the end.
Partner with product and engineering. Translate business problems into ML solutions. Define API contracts with product engineers. Explain your approach clearly to non-ML partners and leave the room with alignment, not confusion.
Evaluate and iterate fast. Build evaluation frameworks, run experiments, and make data-driven decisions about model and system performance. Ship and iterate; don’t wait for perfect.
Ship AI-powered workflows. Put AI to work on your own processes: automate pipelines, build agentic workflows, and contribute reusable skills and context to Checkr’s agentic platform. The expectation is that our teams operate AI-first.

What You Bring

A Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Mathematics, or a related technical field, or equivalent depth from experience
6+ years building software professionally, with at least 2 of those building ML systems that run in production
Strong Python fluency; you write clean, testable, well-structured code with solid OOP instincts. Hands-on experience using LLM APIs in production systems: prompt engineering, structured outputs, function calling, cost management, and evaluation
You’ve built and maintained APIs, worked with CI/CD pipelines, and shipped code that other engineers depend on
Comfort with and enthusiasm for AI-assisted workflows; experience using LLMs, code-generation tools, or agentic systems in production or operational contexts is a strong signal
You use AI tools (Copilot, Claude, etc.) to move faster, but you understand every line they produce. You can spot AI slop and you don’t ship it
An A-player mindset with a strong bias for action: you raise the bar, move with urgency, stay resilient through ambiguity, and take ownership to deliver meaningful outcomes.

Production complexity was already outpacing what engineering teams could manage manually, and AI-generated code is accelerating that gap. You will need to iterate and prototype rapidly based on customer feedback, understand the nuances of production software systems across industries and scale, and build cutting edge AI systems that operate performantly across petabytes of data.

Our FDEs’ primary objective is to own large-scale strategic projects to meaningfully upgrade the core Traversal platform, product, and AI, based on their learnings from deploying Traversal and delivering value to our customers on the field. Lead the design and implementation of scalable, robust backend systems to support AI agents and observability tools.

Collaborate with AI researchers, product engineers, and infrastructure teams to drive cross-cutting upgrades to our core platform and product offerings.

Build long term relationships with customers and proactively identify new opportunities for AI deployment throughout the lifecycle of an engagement.
Be a champion for Traversal’s mission in the field.

3+ years of software engineering experience, with a strong focus on backend, data, and/or cloud infrastructure systems.
